newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says only minor details remain in Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says only minor details remain in Hebron deal.

text.p: Main issues in an Israeli-Palestinian deal over the West Bank town of Hebron have been resolved and only a few minor details are left, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Tuesday.

He was speaking as U.S. and Palestinian officials in the region said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat would meet late on Tuesday to try to clinch an accord.
"The main substantive issues have been resolved. Only a few minor details are left. Exceedingly minor," Burns told Reuters.
"It's time to conclude a deal. The leaders are the only ones who can make these decisions to complete the Hebron agreement," he added.
But another U.S. official, asked if an agreement would be concluded on Tuesday, said: "I won't predict anything ... It's the Middle East."

Hebron, a West Bank flashpoint, is home to 400 militant Jewish settlers and 100,000 Arabs. It was to be handed over to the Palestinians last March but violence, security concerns and Israel's change of government in June delayed the pullback.
It is the last of seven Palestinian cities that were to be turned over to Palestinian self-rule under a 1995 interim peace accord signed by the previous Israeli government.
